subject: CS Graphical Visual Computing
title: Prelim Exam — Principles of Animation, Design & Web Basics

questions.text: Which animation principle is considered the most important and gives objects the illusion of weight by deforming while keeping volume constant?
questions.hint: Think of a bouncing ball — it flattens on impact and stretches in the air.

questions.text: A character winds up before throwing a punch. Which animation principle does this demonstrate?
questions.hint: It prepares the viewer's eye for what is about to happen.

questions.text: Which animation principle states that almost all living motion follows a curved path rather than a straight line?
questions.hint: Think about how a hand naturally swings — it never moves in a perfectly straight line.

questions.text: A character's coat continues to sway briefly after the character stops walking. Which principle does this illustrate?
questions.hint: Loose parts don't stop at the same time as the main body.

questions.text: Which animation principle directly corresponds to CSS properties like ease-in and ease-out?
questions.hint: Objects accelerate gradually and decelerate naturally — more frames at the start and end.

questions.text: Which principle refers to the overall quality that makes a character pleasant and interesting to watch — even if they are a villain?
questions.hint: It's not about being likable — it's about being watchable.

questions.text: Fast timing in animation tends to read as which of the following?
questions.hint: Think of a cartoon slap — it happens in a flash.

questions.text: Which principle ensures the audience's eye is directed to the right place at the right time — like a clear, readable silhouette?
questions.hint: Present one clear idea at a time — like a theater spotlight.

questions.text: Which design principle explains why a bright-colored button does not get lost in a wall of body text?
questions.hint: Difference in color, size, or weight creates emphasis.

questions.text: The 60-30-10 rule — 60% dominant, 30% secondary, 10% accent — belongs to which design principle?
questions.hint: It keeps a palette from feeling chaotic.

questions.text: A layout that uses the same visual weight on both sides of a centerline is an example of which type of balance?
questions.hint: It looks mirrored — formal and trustworthy.

questions.text: Which design principle states that every element on a page should line up with something else, creating invisible structure?
questions.hint: Nothing should sit randomly on the page.

questions.text: Which design principle is described as the fastest way to make a design feel premium?
questions.hint: Beginners fear this and rush to fill it — don't.

questions.text: Websites are commonly built on an invisible skeleton of how many columns to keep alignment consistent?
questions.hint: Think of it as graph paper beneath the design.

questions.text: Which best describes a wireframe?
options: A fully interactive prototype with animations
A high-fidelity design with full colors and typography
A low-fidelity skeletal blueprint focused on layout and structure
questions.hint: No colors, no real fonts — just boxes and placeholders.

questions.text: What is the key difference between a mockup and a prototype?
options: A mockup has color; a prototype does not
A mockup is interactive; a prototype is static
A mockup is static; a prototype is interactive
There is no difference between the two
questions.hint: You can click through a prototype but not a mockup.

questions.text: Which HTML tag creates the largest heading on a page?
questions.hint: h1 through h6 — the number goes up as importance goes down.

questions.text: In the CSS Box Model, which property controls the space outside an element's border?
questions.hint: Padding is inside the border — this one is outside.

questions.text: Which is the best practice for adding CSS to an HTML page?
options: Inline styles using the style attribute
questions.hint: It's reusable across multiple pages and keeps concerns separated.

questions.text: Which JavaScript method is used to select an element by its ID and change its displayed content?
questions.hint: It uses the element's unique id attribute to find and modify it.

questions.text: The principle of Squash & Stretch requires that an object's volume remain constant — if it stretches taller, it must get thinner.
questions.hint: Volume conservation is the core rule of this principle.

questions.text: Slow In & Slow Out means an animated object maintains a constant speed from start to finish.
questions.hint: Real objects accelerate and decelerate — they do NOT move at constant speed.

questions.text: Secondary Action is a supporting motion that adds richness to a scene without competing with or distracting from the main action.
questions.hint: Think of a character nodding their head while walking — the walk is primary.

questions.text: The Straight Ahead animation method is more controlled and planned than the Pose to Pose method.
questions.hint: Straight Ahead is spontaneous — Pose to Pose is the planned, controlled approach.

questions.text: In the 13 Principles of Design, Proximity means that related items should be placed close together to show they belong to the same group.
questions.hint: Closeness communicates relationship — no labels or borders needed.

questions.text: Accessibility is considered an optional extra feature that only needs to be addressed after the main design is complete.
questions.hint: If it only works for some users, it isn't finished — it's a baseline, not a bonus.

questions.text: Asymmetrical balance uses different elements of similar visual weight to create a dynamic and modern feel.
questions.hint: It doesn't mirror — it balances using contrast and variety instead.

questions.text: A mockup is interactive — users can click buttons and navigate between screens to test the flow.
questions.hint: That describes a prototype. A mockup looks real but does nothing when clicked.

questions.text: In CSS, the class selector uses a dot (.) prefix, while the ID selector uses a hash (#) prefix.
questions.hint: .box targets a class — #box targets a unique ID.

questions.text: In HTML, the <body> tag contains meta-information such as the page title and linked stylesheets.
questions.hint: Meta-information goes inside <head> — <body> holds the visible content.
